name: unittest-loop
description: Generate unit tests for existing code: pick the seam -> enumerate the cases -> write -> prove the tests catch defects
pattern: generator + mutation check (a test going red when the code breaks is the evaluator)
whenToUse: Tests are needed for working code: raising coverage, backfilling after a feature, or before a refactor.
whenNotToUse: There is a bug with an unknown cause -> use fixbug-loop; the red test is produced there.

steps.goal: Reuse the test infrastructure that exists, do not build new
outputs: An existing test file read as the template
steps.exitCriteria: HW.UnitTests/TestSupport/ has been read, plus at least the test file nearest the area under test
steps.note: There is no Moq/NSubstitute/FluentAssertions in the project. Plain xUnit asserts + hand-written stubs.

steps.goal: Test through the same door production goes through
steps.exitCriteria: entity -> call directly | handler -> VocabTestHarness | validator -> Validate() | agent tool -> StubSender
steps.note: Feeling that you 'need a mock' almost always means you are testing at the wrong seam.

steps.goal: List the cases BEFORE typing code
outputs: Case table across the 4 groups: happy | boundary | error | preservation
steps.exitCriteria: All 4 groups, or an explicit statement of which group was skipped and why
steps.note: The 'preservation' group (does what must NOT change actually stay unchanged) is the most often skipped and catches the most bugs.

steps.exitCriteria: One behaviour per test. The test name is a claim about behaviour. Never assert on a random value.
steps.note: test-writer must NOT change production code. A test red because the code is wrong is a FINDING.

steps.goal: Prove the tests are not decoration
outputs: Evidence: break the production code -> the test goes RED for the right reason -> revert -> GREEN
steps.exitCriteria: Done for at least one important test, or stated plainly that it could not be done
steps.note: Skip this step and the whole suite is decoration. Coverage measures which lines RAN, not which behaviour was ASSERTED.

steps.exitCriteria: PASS. Randomness involved -> re-run 3 times; red 1 time in 3 is a broken test, not bad luck.

stopConditions.rule: the same test fails 3 times for the same reason
stopConditions.action: Pick ONE: change seam | narrow the case | stop and report (red because the CODE is wrong -> hand to /fixbug)
Stop. Record it under 'Red because the code is wrong', do not fix it yourself.
